result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers find the same core problems: small text, very long lines, tight line height, negative letter-spacing, little space between paragraphs and list items, and weak heading hierarchy. Both give concrete replacement values. A wins because it keeps the existing typeface and colors and uses rem units that respect users' browser settings. B changes the font stack and sets a text color in its CSS, which the rubric counts as drift, though B does rank line length as the biggest cause more clearly. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers spot all five typographic problems and give concrete values: 16px body text, a capped text column, about 1.5–1.6 line height, more space above headings than below, and no negative letter-spacing. Answer A ranks its fixes more clearly, calling line length the biggest cause. But it changes the typeface to system-ui and sets a new text color, which the rubric counts against it. Answer B keeps Arial and only suggests checking the color, and its rem units also respect users' browser text-size settings.
